title: Name the frequency ratio
spoken: q is defined as the moving frequency over the stationary frequency.
explanation: q is a name for how much the frequency changes: the moving system's frequency divided by the stationary system's, for the same light.
assumptions: The moving system moves along x at speed v relative to the stationary system, with |v| < c. Modern teaching notation: gamma is the paper's beta, c its V.
A plane light wave whose direction makes the angle phi with the direction of motion, in the stationary system.
The same wave phase, written in both systems' coordinates, fixes frequency and direction together.

notes.title: Divide one by the other
notes.explanation: Both are frequencies of the same light, so the units cancel.

notes.title: A definition
notes.explanation: This line names q; the next one says what q is.

notes.title: Frequency in the stationary system
notes.explanation: Crests per second as the stationary system's clocks count them.

notes.title: Frequency in the moving system
notes.explanation: Crests per second as the moving system's clocks count them.

notes.title: The frequency ratio
notes.explanation: A pure number. Greater than 1 means the moving system counts more crests per second.

sentence.text: the frequency in the moving system
the frequency in the stationary system
